q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'Supplementary Grant' from an 'Excess Grant'?

options.A: A Supplementary Grant is voted after the year ends, whereas an Excess Grant is voted during the year
options.B: Both are voted before any expenditure is incurred
options.C: A Supplementary Grant is obtained during the financial year when the amount already granted for a service proves insufficient, whereas an Excess Grant is obtained after the close of the year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of the grant
options.D: A Supplementary Grant needs no vote of Parliament, whereas an Excess Grant is charged on the Consolidated Fund

q: A 'token' provision is made in a Demand for Grants for a new work or service when:

options.A: The funds required for the work or service during the year are intended to be found by re-appropriation from savings within the grant, the token provision being made to obtain the approval of Parliament to the new item
options.B: The work is to be financed entirely from market borrowings
options.C: The expenditure is charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.D: The work has already been completed in the previous year

q: The apportionment of through-traffic earnings is carried out among the zonal railways every month. Its net effect on the total gross earnings of the Indian Railways taken as a whole is that the total:

options.A: Increases by the amount of terminal charges collected
options.B: Decreases by the amount held under Traffic Suspense
options.C: Is shared equally among all the zonal railways
options.D: Remains unchanged, apportionment merely distributing the same earnings among the railways over which the traffic has passed

q: A through passenger ticket is issued for a journey which passes over two zonal railways of unequal length. In the apportionment of the coaching earnings from this ticket, the share of each railway is worked out broadly in proportion to:

options.A: The number of coaches owned by each railway
options.B: The distance over which the passenger is carried on each railway
options.C: The number of originating passengers booked on each railway
options.D: The capital-at-charge of each railway

q: The earnings from parcels and luggage booked by coaching trains on a zonal railway are taken to account, for the purpose of apportionment in the Traffic Book, under:

options.A: Part A of the Traffic Book, which deals with Coaching earnings
options.B: Part B of the Traffic Book, which deals with Goods earnings
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings, which are never apportioned
options.D: The Public Account of India

q: In the allocation of an item of capital expenditure on a zonal railway, the elements of the allocation string, read in order, broadly indicate:

options.A: Only the name of the contractor to whom payment is to be made
options.B: The source of finance (fund), the Plan Head of the work and the Primary Unit (object) of expenditure
options.C: Only the month in which the expenditure was incurred
options.D: Only the division in which the work is situated

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Railway Pension Fund is credited by appropriation from revenue.
2. The pensionary charges of the Railways are met by debit to the Railway Pension Fund.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: The Capital Fund of the Railways is credited mainly with appropriations made out of:

options.A: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.B: The safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.C: The deposits of contractors held in the Public Account
options.D: The surplus of the Railways, after meeting dividend (while it was payable) and other charges, available for financing capital works from internal resources

q: If the annual appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is kept persistently below the level warranted by the renewals falling due, the consequence in the railway accounts and working is that:

options.A: Arrears of renewals and replacements accumulate, affecting the condition and safety of assets, even though the working expenses of the year appear lower
options.B: The Operating Ratio of the year automatically becomes more favourable in a real sense
options.C: The balance in the Pension Fund increases correspondingly
options.D: The capital-at-charge of the Railways is reduced by the amount of under-provision

q: A zonal railway takes up the elimination of a level crossing by constructing a road over-bridge as a safety work and proposes to finance works of this class from the fund credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares and a share of the cess on diesel and petrol. That fund is the:

options.A: Capital Fund
options.B: Railway Safety Fund
options.C: Debt Service Fund
options.D: Development Fund

q: A zonal railway proposes the renewal and upgradation of signalling and track assets which have become due for replacement on safety considerations, and seeks finance from the dedicated safety corpus created in the Budget of 2017-18 for safety-related works of renewal, replacement and upgradation. The fund referred to is the:

options.A: Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.B: Railway Safety Fund
options.C: Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.D: Capital Fund

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the General Books from the Subsidiary Books of a zonal railway?

options.A: The General Books record only stores transactions, whereas the Subsidiary Books record only cash transactions
options.B: Both sets of books are rendered monthly to the Railway Board
options.C: The General Books are maintained only in the workshops, whereas the Subsidiary Books are maintained only at stations
options.D: The Subsidiary Books record the transactions in detail in the first instance, whereas the General Books record the compiled and classified results posted from the subsidiary books and summaries

q: To accommodate the large number of year-end adjustments, the Account Current of a zonal railway for the month of March is rendered in two parts, which are known as the:

options.A: March (Preliminary) Account Current and the March (Final) Account Current
options.B: March Account Current and the April Account Current
options.C: Approximate Account Current and the Single Account Current
options.D: Revenue Account Current and the Capital Account Current

q: Inter-railway transfer transactions of the zonal railways, after acceptance, are finally adjusted and cleared through the head 'Transfer Railways' maintained in the books of:

options.A: The Reserve Bank of India at Nagpur
options.B: The Railway Board
options.C: The Pay and Accounts Office of the Ministry of Finance
options.D: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India

q: In the books of a zonal railway, the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' is operated to record:

options.A: The Provident Fund subscriptions recovered from the staff
options.B: The cheques issued by the railway but not yet encashed
options.C: The amounts remitted by the Cash Office and stations into the accredited bank, pending their adjustment against 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'
options.D: The transfer certificates issued to other railways

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Appropriation Act from the Appropriation Accounts?

options.A: The Appropriation Act is prepared by the C&AG, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are passed by Parliament
options.B: Both are prepared by the zonal railways at the close of the year
options.C: The Appropriation Act is an accounts document, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are a law
options.D: The Appropriation Act is the law passed by Parliament authorising withdrawal of moneys from the Consolidated Fund up to the amounts granted, whereas the Appropriation Accounts are the accounts prepared after the close of the year comparing the actual expenditure with the final grant

q: The 'Final Grant' of a zonal railway for a financial year represents:

options.A: The original grant as voted by Parliament, together with supplementary grants obtained and as modified by re-appropriations sanctioned during the year
options.B: Only the Budget Estimates as originally presented to Parliament
options.C: Only the Revised Estimates as framed in September
options.D: The grant of the following year taken on account

q: The Operating Ratio of the Railways for a year broadly expresses:

options.A: The ratio of capital expenditure to revenue expenditure of the year
options.B: The ratio of the working expenses of the year to the gross earnings of the year, expressed as a percentage
options.C: The ratio of goods earnings to coaching earnings of the year
options.D: The ratio of the Pension Fund balance to the total pensionary charges

q: The Net Revenue of the Railways for a financial year is arrived at by deducting, from the gross earnings of the year:

options.A: Only the dividend payable to General Revenues
options.B: Only the capital expenditure incurred during the year
options.C: The total working expenses of the year, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund
options.D: The total balances held under the suspense heads at the close of the year

q: The balance under Stores Suspense, exhibited under Plan Head 71 in the capital classification, broadly represents:

options.A: The amounts recoverable from staff for stores lost in transit
options.B: The cheques issued for stores purchases but not yet encashed
options.C: The earnings of stores depots from the sale of scrap
options.D: The value of stores in stock with the Railways, purchased and held pending issue for works and maintenance

q: A workshop accountant proposes to book the labour and material locked up on unfinished jobs under Plan Head 71, which covers Stores Suspense. The correct position is that such balances on jobs in progress belong to:

options.A: Manufacturing Suspense under Plan Head 72
options.B: Stores Suspense under Plan Head 71
options.C: Miscellaneous Advances under Plan Head 73
options.D: Other Specified Works under Plan Head 64

q: The earnings collected at a station of a zonal railway pass, in their journey to final adjustment in the Government accounts, broadly through the sequence:

options.A: Station, Railway Board, Ministry of Finance
options.B: Station, Cash Office of the railway, accredited bank and the Central Accounts Section of the Reserve Bank at Nagpur
options.C: Station, Pay and Accounts Office, Comptroller and Auditor General
options.D: Station, Traffic Accounts Office, Railway Board

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the focal point system from Door Step Banking for the remittance of station earnings?

options.A: Under both systems, station staff carry cash personally to the Reserve Bank at Nagpur
options.B: The focal point system applies only to goods earnings, whereas Door Step Banking applies only to coaching earnings
options.C: Under the focal point system, stations remit their earnings to the nominated focal point branch of the accredited bank, whereas under Door Step Banking the bank collects the earnings from the railway premises itself
options.D: The focal point system has been replaced by the Traffic Book, whereas Door Step Banking has been replaced by E-Recon

q: The principal advantage claimed for E-Recon of transfer transactions between railways is that it:

options.A: Dispenses with the need for the respondent railway to accept a transaction
options.B: Converts all transfer transactions into cash transactions
options.C: Abolishes the head 'Transfer Railways' altogether
options.D: Enables transfer transactions raised by one railway to be matched and accepted by the respondent railway electronically and promptly, reducing the outstandings under 'Transfer Railways'

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Subdivision I of the Development Fund (DF-I) is meant for works of passenger and other railway user amenities.
2. Subdivision III of the Development Fund (DF-III) is meant for unremunerative operational improvement works.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

q: During a year, a zonal railway collects rent for railway land given on licence, licence fees for the use of railway buildings and charges for advertisements displayed at stations. As these receipts are local and miscellaneous in nature and do not arise from traffic carried over more than one railway, they are taken to account as:

options.A: Other Coaching Earnings and apportioned among all railways
options.B: Goods earnings and apportioned in proportion to distance
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings accruing wholly to that railway
options.D: Receipts of the Public Account of India

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'originating earnings' from 'apportioned earnings' of a zonal railway?

options.A: Originating earnings are the earnings initially collected and accounted for by the railway on which the traffic originates, whereas apportioned earnings are the share of the through-traffic earnings finally due to that railway after apportionment among all the railways concerned
options.B: Originating earnings relate only to goods traffic, whereas apportioned earnings relate only to coaching traffic
options.C: Both expressions denote the earnings held under Traffic Suspense
options.D: Originating earnings are credited to the Railway Board, whereas apportioned earnings are credited to the Reserve Bank

q: The expenditure on the ordinary working expenses of the Railways, provided for in the Demands for Grants, is an example of:

options.A: Charged expenditure on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.B: Voted expenditure, voted by the Lok Sabha as part of the Demands for Grants
options.C: Expenditure from the Public Account requiring no appropriation
options.D: Expenditure met from the Contingency Fund of India

q: A proposal is made to meet a shortfall under a revenue head of a zonal railway by re-appropriation from a capital head where savings are available. The correct position is that re-appropriation:

options.A: Is freely permissible between revenue and capital heads with the sanction of the General Manager
options.B: Is permissible between revenue and capital heads with the sanction of the Principal Financial Adviser
options.C: Is not permissible between the revenue and capital sections of a grant, nor between voted and charged expenditure
options.D: Is permissible only at the Final Modification Estimates stage in January

q: A zonal railway finds, in November, that the grant for a service will be exhausted before the close of the year and that further funds will be needed during the same year. The requirement is correctly placed before Parliament during the year itself through:

options.A: An Excess Grant
options.B: A Vote of Credit
options.C: The Appropriation Accounts of the previous year
options.D: Supplementary Demands for Grants

q: A clerk is unable to incorporate a railway transaction directly in the Government accounts because the commercial accounts of the Railways are maintained in a different form from the Government accounts. options.A: Link heads
options.B: Token grants
options.C: Budget proportions
options.D: Transfer certificates

q: At the monthly review of outstandings, the Accounts Office of a zonal railway examines a report which lists the balances lying under the Provident Fund, deposits, suspense and remittance heads, so that old outstandings can be pursued. This report is the:

options.A: Pink Book
options.B: Debt Head Report
options.C: Traffic Book
options.D: Works Register

q: The monthly Account Current rendered by a zonal railway is compiled from:

options.A: Only the station balance sheets received during the month
options.B: Only the Cash Book of the Cash and Pay Office
options.C: The Budget Estimates of the railway for the year
options.D: The General Books of the railway for the month, which embody the classified transactions of that month

q: Along with the Revised Estimates for the current year framed in September, a zonal railway is required to frame, at the same stage, the:

options.A: Appropriation Accounts for the previous year
options.B: Final Modification Estimates for the current year
options.C: Excess Grants for the previous year
options.D: Budget Estimates for the ensuing year

q: The Provident Fund subscriptions recovered every month from the salaries of railway staff are held by the Government in trust for the staff and are accordingly accounted for in:

options.A: The Public Account of India, under the Provident Fund heads including Major Head 8009 for the State Railway Provident Fund
options.B: The Consolidated Fund of India as revenue receipts of the Railways
options.C: The Contingency Fund of India
options.D: The Railway Pension Fund under the capital classification

q: In the Accounts Office of a zonal railway, a bill received from an executive department is first entered in detail, transaction by transaction, before any classified summary is prepared from it. The books in which transactions are so recorded in detail in the first instance are the:

options.A: Subsidiary Books
options.B: General Books
options.C: Appropriation Accounts
options.D: Works Programme

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Ledger of a zonal railway is one of its General Books.

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2
options.C: 2 only
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

options.A: The station balance sheets received during the month only

options.C: The General Books of the railway for the month
options.D: The Budget Register of the railway for the year

q: At the close of a month, the Accounts Office of a zonal railway prepares a consolidated statement showing the outstanding balances under the Provident Fund, deposits, suspense and remittance heads, so that old outstandings under each head can be chased for clearance. This statement is the:

options.A: Works Register
options.B: Budget Register
options.C: Traffic Book
options.D: Debt Head Report

q: A surprise check of the imprest held by an officer is carried out. The cash physically found with the holder, together with the paid vouchers held by him awaiting recoupment, should together equal:

options.A: The sanctioned amount of the imprest
options.B: The contingent expenditure of the previous month

q: A debit balance under the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' in the books of a zonal railway represents:

options.A: Cheques issued by the railway which have not yet been paid by the bank

options.C: Provident Fund balances awaiting investment

q: A cheque issued by a zonal railway in March is paid by the bank in April. The item is cleared from the suspense head 'Cheques and Bills' in the railway books:

options.A: On the date the cheque is issued by the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: On the date the payee receives the cheque
options.C: When the bank's intimation or advice of payment of the cheque is received
options.D: Automatically at the close of the financial year

q: Balances outstanding under the suspense head 'Reserve Bank Suspense' in the books of a zonal railway are cleared:

options.A: By write-off under the sanction of the General Manager
options.B: Automatically at the end of five years
options.C: Only after the statutory audit of the year is completed
options.D: On receipt of the advice or intimation from the Reserve Bank of India

q: A transaction between a zonal railway and a State Government, routed through the Accountant General of the State, is pending clearance in the railway books. Pending clearance, the transaction is held under the suspense head:

options.D: Cheques and Bills

q: Goods and services have been received by a zonal railway from an outside supplier, but payment to the supplier is still to be made. Pending payment, the amount due is credited to the head:

options.A: Demands Recoverable

options.C: Demands Payable
options.D: Reserve Bank Suspense

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes a 'debt head' from a 'suspense head' in the railway accounts?

options.C: A debt head relates only to capital works, whereas a suspense head relates only to revenue works

q: An outside party deposits money with a zonal railway for a work to be executed by the railway on the party's behalf, and the deposit is credited to the 'Deposits' head. The expenditure incurred on that deposit work is:

options.C: Remitted to the Railway Board as its receipt

options.A: An Excess Grant after the close of the year
options.B: A Vote of Credit under Article 116
options.C: A token supplementary demand for a nominal amount
options.D: No demand at all, as re-appropriation by itself is sufficient

q:
Consider the following statements:

options.A: 1 only
options.B: Both 1 and 2

options.A: Retained till the last day of the financial year

options.C: Spent on any other work selected by the executive
options.D: Carried forward automatically to the next financial year

options.A: Railway Safety Fund
